evals.query: Create a new Kora service in Java from scratch with Gradle.
expected_behavior: Creates build.gradle with the java and application plugins
Imports the BOM via koraBom platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:$koraVersion") declared once
Pins koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2 and resolves it from plain mavenCentral()
Adds annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors"
Defines an @KoraApp interface as the graph root
Does not version individual io.koraframework:* artifacts
Does not put 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT in the project, and does not add the Sonatype snapshot repository
Does not use the removed ru.tinkoff.kora group or the kora-parent BOM
Does not use foreign-framework annotations or field injection

evals.query: Set up the Gradle configurations so the Kora annotation processor resolves with the right version.
expected_behavior: Declares a custom koraBom configuration
Wires annotationProcessor.extendsFrom(koraBom) so the processor classpath gets the BOM
Extends implementation, compileOnly, and the test configurations from koraBom
Explains the annotation-processor classpath is separate from the application classpath
Does not put an explicit version on the io.koraframework:annotation-processors dependency

evals.query: Write the main application class that boots the Kora graph.
expected_behavior: Annotates the interface with @KoraApp imported from io.koraframework.common.annotation.KoraApp
Extends framework *Module interfaces such as UndertowPublicHttpServerModule and HoconConfigModule
Calls KoraApplication.run(ApplicationGraph::graph) in main
Imports KoraApplication from io.koraframework.application.graph
Explains the generated graph class is the interface simple name plus Graph, in the same package
Does not import @KoraApp from io.koraframework.common (the annotation lives one package deeper)
Does not reference a foreign-framework application-bootstrap annotation

evals.query: My Kora Java build produces no generated code and ApplicationGraph cannot be resolved.
expected_behavior: Identifies the missing annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" as the cause
Notes that the graph class is generated from the @KoraApp interface at compile time
Suggests running ./gradlew classes to trigger the processor
Points to build/generated/sources/annotationProcessor/ for the generated graph
Mentions verifying the processor classpath with ./gradlew dependencies --configuration annotationProcessor

evals.query: My build.gradle has annotationProcessor "ru.tinkoff.kora:annotation-processors" and implementation "ru.tinkoff.kora:json-module" with platform("ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent:1.2.19"). Gradle cannot resolve anything. Fix it for Kora 2.0.
expected_behavior: Replaces the group ru.tinkoff.kora with io.koraframework on every coordinate
Replaces the kora-parent BOM with io.koraframework:kora-bom at 2.0.0.RC2
Replaces json-module with json-common (json-module does not exist in 2.0)
Keeps the processor artifact name annotation-processors and leaves it unversioned under the BOM
Does not keep the artifact name kora-parent under the new group: io.koraframework:kora-parent exists on Central only as a 2.0.0.alpha leftover and is not part of the 2.0 releases
Does not invent a 2.0 coordinate for a module that was removed

evals.query: Which JDK and Gradle version should I use for a Kora Java project, and how do I configure the toolchain?
expected_behavior: States that Kora 2.0 artifacts are compiled for JVM 25, so 25 is the floor
Configures the Java toolchain with JavaLanguageVersion.of(25) in build.gradle
Adds the foojay-resolver-convention plugin in settings.gradle
Pins the Gradle wrapper at 9.8.0, the version the Kora framework builds with
Does not claim --enable-preview is required for consumers of Kora 2.0

evals.query: Configuration fails with 'Dependency requires at least JVM runtime version 25. This build uses a Java 21 JVM.' My toolchain already says JavaLanguageVersion.of(25).
expected_behavior: Explains the toolchain does not control the JVM that runs Gradle itself
Identifies the buildscript classpath (io.koraframework:openapi-generator) as what is resolved by the Gradle JVM
Tells the user to run Gradle on JDK 25 or newer, e.g. via JAVA_HOME
Advises against committing org.gradle.java.home because the path is machine-specific
Does not suggest lowering the toolchain or excluding the dependency

evals.query: After moving my project to Kora 2.0 the build reports hundreds of 'package ru.tinkoff.kora.common.annotation does not exist' errors in files I never wrote, all under build/generated.
expected_behavior: Identifies stale generator output left in build/generated as the cause
Explains generator tasks do not delete previous output and the build cache key ignores the package change
Prescribes ./gradlew clean followed by a build with --no-build-cache
Does not suggest editing the generated sources
Does not treat the error as a missing dependency

evals.query: Add the Gradle setup so I can write a @KoraAppTest for my new Kora service.
expected_behavior: Adds testImplementation "io.koraframework:test-junit5"
Adds testAnnotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors"
Enables useJUnitPlatform() in the test task
Uses @KoraAppTest with @TestComponent imported from io.koraframework.test.extension.junit5
Does not use a foreign-framework test annotation or a mock-bean construct

evals.query: I scaffolded a Kora app; how do I actually expose an HTTP endpoint?
expected_behavior: Adds implementation "io.koraframework:http-server-undertow"
Extends UndertowPublicHttpServerModule in the @KoraApp interface
Creates a @Component @HttpController with an @HttpRoute method returning HttpServerResponse
Configures httpServer.port and httpServer.system.port in application.conf
Uses constructor injection rather than field injection
Does not use the removed publicApiHttpPort / privateApiHttpPort config keys

evals.query: My application.conf sets httpServer.publicApiHttpPort = 8090 and httpServer.privateApiHttpPort = 8091 but the service still answers on 8080 and 8085.
expected_behavior: Explains those keys do not exist in Kora 2.0 config, so the defaults apply
Gives the 2.0 keys: httpServer.port and httpServer.system.port
Mentions the system API defaults: port 8085 serving /system/readiness, /system/liveness and /metrics
States SystemHttpServerConfig overrides port() to 8085 rather than inheriting 8080, so the two servers do not collide
Does not claim a port conflict or an 'address already in use' failure

evals.query: Compilation fails with 'type annotation @org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable is not expected here' after I annotated a nested type. Also, can I keep using jakarta.annotation.Nullable?
expected_behavior: States Kora 2.0 uses JSpecify and that its annotations are type-use
Shows the correct position on a qualified nested type: Outer.@Nullable Inner
Notes the array and generic positions differ in meaning
States jakarta.annotation.Nullable is not what Kora 2.0 uses
Does not suggest suppressing the error or removing nullability information

evals.query: My new Kora service starts fine but there are no request logs and no http_server_* metrics. Nothing is misconfigured as far as I can tell.
expected_behavior: Explains component telemetry logging and metrics default to false in Kora 2.0
Shows enabling httpServer.telemetry.logging.enabled and httpServer.telemetry.metrics.enabled
Notes metrics additionally need a MeterRegistry in the graph (micrometer-module)
Does not state tracing is enabled everywhere: the system server overrides tracing enabled() to false under httpServer.system
Does not claim telemetry is on by default

evals.query: We package our Kora 2.0 service as a fat jar with the com.gradleup.shadow 9 plugin and `shadowJar { mergeServiceFiles() }`. `./gradlew run` works, but `java -jar app-all.jar` dies during Flyway migration with a NullPointerException in DryRunConfigurationExtensionStub.getOrResolveOutputStream. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Identifies the META-INF/services merge: with Shadow 9.x the default duplicates strategy keeps only the first copy of each service file, so mergeServiceFiles() has nothing to merge
Explains that Flyway registers plugins via ServiceLoader in both flyway-core and flyway-database-postgresql, so the fat jar loses some of them
Gives the fix: duplicatesStrategy = DuplicatesStrategy.INCLUDE on shadowJar together with mergeServiceFiles()
Presents this as an empirically observed packaging behaviour, not a Kora defect, and mentions the distTar layout the reference apps use as the alternative
Does not suggest downgrading Flyway or disabling the Kora Flyway module
